one_line: A silent 29-second Lovevery clip where an adult slowly demonstrates a wooden disc puzzle to a toddler while on-screen text spells out the 'SHOW' teaching method (Slow Hands Omit Words), ending on the toddler clapping.

hook.visual: Toddler in a light-blue sweater sits on a grey carpet beside a wooden puzzle board with photo faces and loose coloured discs; an adult hand enters from the bottom-right and touches the board.
hook.on_screen_text: Giving instructions the Montessori way: / S / H / O / W (letters stacked vertically; they fill in word by word: 'Slow', 'Slow Hands', 'Slow Hands Omit', 'Slow Hands Omit Words') (English on screen, no translation needed)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: A real toddler in a lived-in room plus four big stacked letters that clearly spell out something. The viewer wants to see what S-H-O-W stands for, and the answer is revealed one word every 1.5 s, which keeps them for the first 7.5 s.

beats.observed: Toddler watches the board while an adult hand reaches in and presses a disc into the third slot. The header 'Giving instructions the Montessori way:' sits at the top; the vertical letters S H O W are shown, with the first word 'Slow' appearing at 1.5 s and 'Slow Hands' at 3.0 s.
beats.on_screen_text: Giving instructions the Montessori way: / S H O W, then 'Slow', 'Slow Hands'

beats.observed: The adult hand moves discs slowly and deliberately while the toddler watches and leans in. The acronym completes: 'Slow Hands Omit' at 4.5 s, 'Slow Hands Omit Words' at 6.0 s. By 7.5 s the hand is pulling out of frame.
No adult hand in frame. Toddler sits holding an orange disc in the lap; the board shows only face photos and the remaining discs lie on the carpet.

Toddler explores alone: presses the orange disc into slots, leans across the board, reaches for a small yellow disc. A white caption box appears at about 10.5 s. An adult hand re-enters briefly at the bottom-right edge around 13.5 to 16.5 s.
beats.on_screen_text: Then sit back and allow them to explore the material.

beats.observed: Toddler tries discs in slots that do not match (a yellow disc in the fourth slot, a pink disc pushed into the second slot at about 21 s) and the board is nudged around. A blurred adult hand moves at the bottom-right at 22.5 and 24 s.
beats.on_screen_text: Allow mistakes. / Allow them to self-correct.

beats.observed: Discs now sit in the board in size order, pink to yellow. Toddler sits back, claps both hands and grins widely at 27.0 and 28.5 s.
beats.spoken: Whisper marks (clapping) at 26.0 to 28.26 s, consistent with the clapping seen in the frames. No speech.
beats.on_screen_text: Watch how proud they feel when they figure it out (with a teary-smile emoji)

payoff: The toddler's proud clapping reaction at 25.5 to 28.5 s, plus the full acronym (Slow Hands Omit Words) completed by 6.0 s.
cta: none on screen or in speech. The caption only credits @casadecullen.
share_or_comment_trigger: A parent can save it as a one-line teaching rule (SHOW) and the clapping toddler is a pure feel-good moment. Likes (1,120) far outnumber shares (25) and comments (3), so it triggers a like and save more than a send or a discussion.
why_it_worked: 5.28% like rate and 18.2x the account median of 1,168 views (21,200 views): high affinity, organic pattern, driven by the baby reaction.
All teaching is carried by text that builds in step with the action (one word per 1.5 s), so it works with sound off; Whisper found no speech at all.
The emotional payoff (clapping toddler) is held to the last 4 s, which gives a reason to watch to the end (inferred, no watch-time data).
paid_signal: no, like rate is 5.28%, far above the 0.3% level that would suggest paid promotion.

solo_route.how: 1) Film 25 to 30 s of a relative's toddler (12 to 24 months) with the phone locked on a stand at floor height: one adult hand demonstrates slowly, then leaves the frame while the child explores. 2) Use LumeBook's own product as the activity: a personalised board-book preview where the child finds the hero who looks like them, so the clapping payoff doubles as a likeness moment. 3) In CapCut or Canva stack the letters S H O W vertically and reveal each word on a roughly 1.5 s cadence, then add two or three white caption boxes in the same plain style. 4) Put the one-sentence rule in the caption and have a barter child-development or Montessori expert vet the claim before posting.
solo_route.needs: A real toddler with written parental consent, and ideally a barter expert to check the method claim. AI cannot replace the genuine reaction that makes this work.

lumebook_version.concept: A 25 s silent clip with word-by-word on-screen text: an adult slowly turns one page of a LumeBook, steps back, and lets a toddler explore until they spot the hero who looks like them and clap. The caption carries the teaching tip, checked by an expert.

evidence_notes: Observed: the toddler, the puzzle board (a 'LOVEVERY' mark is faintly visible on the board), all on-screen text, the adult hand entering and leaving, the clapping. Spoken: nothing; Whisper returns [Music] for 0 to 26 s and (clapping) for 26.0 to 28.26 s, so there is no usable speech transcript, and I cannot describe the music. The learning claims (observational learning, mental models) come only from the caption, and the 'proud' feeling is an on-screen claim: the frames show a child clapping and smiling, not a feeling. The @casadecullen tag suggests the footage is a creator's, so made_by is inferred as a repost or credit; whether it is a licensed collab is unclear. Frames at 22.5 and 24 s are blurred, so I cannot say what the adult hand is doing.
